Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Visalandra Mahasabha
B. Dhar Commission
C. Swami Sitaram's fast
D. Formation of States Re-organization Commission.
Codes:
x:
The demand for a separate Andhra State and later a Visalandhra gained momentum after Independence through a series of political developments. The Dhar Commission was appointed in 1948 to examine the question of linguistic provinces. It did not recommend the formation of states on a linguistic basis. In 1949, the Visalandra Mahasabha was formed to campaign for the unification of all Telugu-speaking areas into a single state. Swami Sitaram undertook his fast in 1951 demanding the formation of Andhra State, which further intensified the movement. The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was constituted in 1953 under the chairmanship of Justice Fazl Ali to examine the reorganisation of states on linguistic and administrative grounds. Its recommendations eventually led to the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956.
Thus, the correct chronological order is: Dhar Commission → Visalandra Mahasabha → Swami Sitaram's Fast → States Reorganisation Commission
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
